mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds rate increases by more than 0.25 percentage points over the next month, the expected S&P 500 20-day forward return turns negative due to tightened credit conditions affecting corporate financing costs.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25pp in the following month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or flat during the identified FEDFUNDS increase period, with a t-statistic below 1.96.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in employment (PAYEMS) of at least 10,000 jobs for three consecutive months is associated with a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return, reflecting stronger labor market confidence and equity valuation expansion.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly increases for 3 consecutive months each ≥10,000
failure_condition: Over the 60-day horizon, the 20-day ahead returns show no statistically significant correlation (R² < 0.05) with the labor strength signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of over 5% followed by a rebound above the prior month's level predicts a positive S&P 20-day forward return as market interprets the recovery as a bottoming signal.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO drops >5% in a month then rises above previous month's value
regime_hint: Downturn followed by recovery in manufacturing demand
failure_condition: No significant excess returns in the 20-day window following the predicted recovery pattern (p > 0.10 in t-test).

mechanism_narrative: When consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) unexpectedly exceeds 3% in the prior month, the S&P 5-day forward return turns negative as investors anticipate future rate hikes that compress equity valuations.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns remain positive or flat despite the inflation spike, with a confidence interval including zero (95%).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising real yields (inverted Treasury term structure proxy via FEDFUNDS - CPIAUCSL) predict negative S&P 20-day forward returns as investors anticipate economic slowdown.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS - CPIAUCSL shows a sustained monthly decline over 2 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from a baseline of zero returns during the identified yield inversion period (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A two consecutive months of declining unemployment (UNRATE) below 4% signals labor market tightening, which is associated with a positive S&P 60-day forward return as equities benefit from stronger labor demand.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE decreases for 2 consecutive months below 4%
failure_condition: Over the 60-day window, forward returns show no correlation with the unemployment decline (R² < 0.01).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden one-time monthly drop in retail sales (HOUST) of 2% or more accompanied by a rebound the following month predicts a positive S&P 20-day forward return as the market interprets the bounce as stabilization in consumer demand.
candidate_trigger: HOUST drops >2% in a month then rebounds above prior month's value
failure_condition: No significant positive returns in the 20-day window post-rebound (p > 0.15).

mechanism_narrative: When the ratio of industrial production to capacity utilization (INDPRO / HOUST) crosses above 0.85, it indicates underutilized manufacturing capacity and predicts a positive S&P 60-day forward return as market anticipates capacity expansion.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than average during the identified undercapacity regime (p > 0.05).
